  "textEditContent": "# Complete Game Mechanics Analysis via Ghidra\n\n&gt; **Last Updated**: Comprehensive MCP/Ghidra analysis session with function decompilation and data label renaming\n\n## Table of Contents\n1. [Action System Overview](#how-the-game-handles-actions-like-open-door)\n2. [Text Response Selection](#text-response-selection-mechanism)\n3. [Random Rejection Messages](#random-rejection-messages-no-puedo-hacer-eso)\n4. [F8 Action Codes](#f8-action-codes-in-text-data)\n5. [In-Memory State Storage](#in-memory-state-storage)\n6. [Use Item X with Y](#how-use-item-x-with-y-works)\n7. [Resource File (alfred.a)](#alfreds-resource-file-system)\n8. [Key Data Addresses](#key-data-addresses-reference)\n\n---\n\n## How the Game Handles Actions Like \"Open Door\"\n\n### Action System Architecture\n\nThe game uses a **multi-tier dispatch system** based on room types and action contexts:\n\n#### 1. Main Action Entry Point: &#96;handle_hotspot_interaction&#96; (0x000124ad)\n\nWhen the player clicks on a hotspot:\n1. The game displays an **action menu** with available verbs (look, take, use, etc.)\n2. Creates a visual popup with action icons from &#96;action_text_table_ptr&#96;\n3. Waits for the player to select an action\n4. Calls &#96;room_specific_action_dispatcher&#96; with the selected action\n\n#### 2. Room-Specific Action Dispatcher (0x00018562)\n\nThis is the **central routing function** that determines how to handle each action:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;c\nvoid room_specific_action_dispatcher(void) {\n    get_current_room_number();\n    action_pending_flag = 0;\n\n    if (room_flags &amp; 0x01) execute_room_specific_script();\n    if (room_flags &amp; 0x02) handle_conversation_tree();\n    if (room_flags &amp; 0x08) handle_dialog_interaction();\n    if (room_flags &amp; 0x10) dispatch_hotspot_action_by_extra_id();\n    if (room_flags &amp; 0x20) execute_script_table_0x47c10();  // TAKE actions\n    if (room_flags &amp; 0x40) execute_script_table_0x47c18();  // PICK UP actions\n    if (room_flags &amp; 0x80) execute_script_table_0x47cbc();\n    if (room_flags &amp; 0x200) execute_complex_item_script_table();  // USE X WITH Y\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Room flags** determine which dispatch tables are active for each room.\n\n#### 3. Action Dispatch Tables\n\nThe game uses **multiple dispatch tables** that map hotspot IDs to function pointers:\n\n| Table Address | Structure | Purpose |\n|--------------|-----------|---------|\n| &#96;0x00047bf0&#96; | 6 bytes: &#96;[uint16 id, ptr32 func]&#96; | Main hotspot actions |\n| &#96;0x00047c10&#96; | 6 bytes: &#96;[uint16 id, ptr32 func]&#96; | \"Take\" verb actions |\n| &#96;0x00047c18&#96; | 6 bytes: &#96;[uint16 id, ptr32 func]&#96; | \"Pick up\" verb actions |\n| &#96;0x00047d24&#96; | 6 bytes: &#96;[uint16 id, ptr32 func]&#96; | Room-specific scripts |\n| &#96;0x00047e58&#96; | 6 bytes: &#96;[uint16 id, ptr32 func]&#96; | F8 action codes |\n| &#96;0x00048118&#96; | 8 bytes: &#96;[uint16 item1, uint16 item2, ptr32 func]&#96; | Item combinations |\n\n### Example Flow: \"Open Door\"\n\n1. Player clicks on door hotspot\n2. &#96;handle_hotspot_interaction&#96; displays action menu\n3. Player selects \"open\" action\n4. &#96;room_specific_action_dispatcher&#96; is called with action code\n5. Based on room flags, appropriate dispatch function is called\n6. ### Key Discoveries:

1. **Text Selection System** - Text is NOT hardcoded in the EXE. All text is loaded from ALFRED.X files at runtime. A text pointer table is built at `room_sprite_data_ptr + 0x3da` by scanning for `0xFF` and `0xFE` markers.

2. **Random Rejection Messages** - Confirmed as **table-based**:
   - 16 pointers at `0x0004bc1c`
   - Selected via `random() & 0xf`
   - This creates the variety in "No puedo hacer eso" responses

3. **F8 Action Codes** - Format is `[0xF8][id_lo][id_hi]`:
   - Dispatch table at `0x00047e58`
   - 6-byte entries: `[uint16 action_id, ptr32 function]`
   - Used to trigger game actions from text data

4. **In-Memory State Storage**:
   - **Conversation branches**: `0x0004fba4` (4 bytes per room)
   - **Inventory items**: `0x0004fc94` (uint16 array)
   - **Sprite visibility**: Z-depth at sprite+0x21 (`0xFF` = disabled)
   - **Exit enable/disable**: Flag at room exit structure + 0x02
   - **Hotspots**: At `room_sprite_data_ptr + 0x47b` (9 bytes each)

5. **alfred.a** - Resource index file containing offset tables for all numbered alfred.1-b data files

Common::Point calculateWalkTarget(Common::Array<WalkBox> &walkboxes, int x, int y) {
	// Starting point for pathfinding
	int sourceX = x;
	int sourceY = y;

	// TODO: If hovering over a sprite/hotspot, adjust source point to sprite center
	// For now, just use mouse position

	// Find nearest walkable point in walkboxes
	uint32 minDistance = 0xFFFFFFFF;
	Common::Point bestTarget(sourceX, sourceY);

	for (size_t i = 0; i < walkboxes.size(); i++) {

		// Calculate distance from source point to this walkbox (Manhattan distance)
		int dx = 0;
		int dy = 0;

		// Calculate horizontal distance
		if (sourceX < walkboxes[i].x) {
			dx = walkboxes[i].x - sourceX;
		} else if (sourceX > walkboxes[i].x + walkboxes[i].w) {
			dx = sourceX - (walkboxes[i].x + walkboxes[i].w);
		}
		// else: sourceX is inside walkbox horizontally, dx = 0

		// Calculate vertical distance
		if (sourceY < walkboxes[i].y) {
			dy = walkboxes[i].y - sourceY;
		} else if (sourceY > walkboxes[i].y + walkboxes[i].h) {
			dy = sourceY - (walkboxes[i].y + walkboxes[i].h);
		}
		// else: sourceY is inside walkbox vertically, dy = 0

		uint32 distance = dx + dy;

		if (distance < minDistance) {
			minDistance = distance;

			// Calculate target point (nearest point on walkbox to source)
			int targetX = sourceX;
			int targetY = sourceY;

			if (sourceX < walkboxes[i].x) {
				targetX = walkboxes[i].x;
			} else if (sourceX > walkboxes[i].x + walkboxes[i].w) {
				targetX = walkboxes[i].x + walkboxes[i].w;
			}

			if (sourceY < walkboxes[i].y) {
				targetY = walkboxes[i].y;
			} else if (sourceY > walkboxes[i].y + walkboxes[i].h) {
				targetY = walkboxes[i].y + walkboxes[i].h;
			}

			bestTarget.x = targetX;
			bestTarget.y = targetY;
		}
	}

	return bestTarget;
}

Based on the documentation, after Alfred walks to a hotspot, the game determines which direction he should face by comparing his position with the target sprite/hotspot position. Let me provide a clear answer:

After Alfred walks to a hotspot, the game determines which direction he should face by **comparing his final position with the target's position**. This happens in the action queueing system after the walking completes.

From `undefined`:

```c
// After walking, orient Alfred toward the target
if (queued_mouse_hover_state == SPRITE) {
    // Calculate direction to sprite
    if (sprite_x > alfred_x) {
        alfred_facing_direction = 0;  // Right
    } else if (sprite_x < alfred_x) {
        alfred_facing_direction = 1;  // Left
    } else if (sprite_y > alfred_y) {
        alfred_facing_direction = 2;  // Down
    } else {
        alfred_facing_direction = 3;  // Up
    }
}
```

**The process:**

1. **During walking setup**: The game saves which sprite/hotspot was clicked in `queued_mouse_hover_state`
2. **After walking completes**: It compares Alfred's final position with the target's position
3. **Priority order** for determining direction:
   - First checks **horizontal difference** (left/right)
   - Then checks **vertical difference** (up/down)

**Direction values:**
- `0` = Facing Right
- `1` = Facing Left
- `2` = Facing Down
- `3` = Facing Up

So if the sprite is to the right of Alfred, he'll turn right. If it's to the left, he'll turn left. Only if they're horizontally aligned will it check vertical positioning.

Let me start by activating the Ghidra tools and then searching for relevant functions.I'll check Ghidra directly to find how the facing direction is determined after walking to a hotspot. Perfect! I found the actual code. Let me examine the key sections that determine facing direction. I can see there are two main cases:

1. **When target is a sprite** (queued_mouse_hover_state == 1) - starting around `LAB_00017e8a`
2. **When target is a hotspot** (queued_mouse_hover_state == 2)

The logic is more complex than the documentation suggested. It checks Alfred's position and size against the target's bounds. Let me extract the exact algorithm:

**For Sprites (queued_mouse_hover_state == 1):**

```c
if (queued_mouse_hover_state == '\x01') {
    sprite = room_sprite_data_ptr + queued_hotspot_sprite_index * 0x2c;

    // Check if Alfred's left edge is past sprite's right edge
    if (sprite.x + sprite.width < alfred_x_position) {
        alfred_facing_direction = 1;  // Face LEFT
    }
    // Check if Alfred's right edge is before sprite's left edge
    else if ((alfred_x_position + alfred_width - alfred_scale_x) < sprite.x) {
        alfred_facing_direction = 0;  // Face RIGHT
    }
    // Alfred is horizontally overlapping with sprite
    else {
        // Check if Alfred's top is above sprite's bottom OR Alfred is within sprite's Y range
        if (((alfred_y_position + alfred_height - alfred_scale_y) < sprite.y) ||
            (alfred_y_position <= sprite.y + sprite.height &&
             sprite.z_depth <= ((399 - alfred_y_position) / 2) + 10)) {
            alfred_facing_direction = 2;  // Face DOWN
        }
        else {
            alfred_facing_direction = 3;  // Face UP
        }
    }
}
```

**For Hotspots (queued_mouse_hover_state == 2):**

```c
if (queued_mouse_hover_state == '\x02') {
    hotspot = room_sprite_data_ptr + queued_hotspot_sprite_index * 9 + 0x47d;

    // Check if Alfred's left edge is past hotspot's right edge
    if (hotspot.x + hotspot.width < alfred_x_position) {
        alfred_facing_direction = 1;  // Face LEFT
    }
    // Check if Alfred's right edge is before hotspot's left edge
    else if ((alfred_x_position + alfred_width - alfred_scale_x) < hotspot.x) {
        alfred_facing_direction = 0;  // Face RIGHT
    }
    // Check vertical positioning
    else if (((alfred_y_position + alfred_height - alfred_scale_y) < hotspot.y) ||
             (alfred_y_position <= hotspot.y + hotspot.height &&
              (hotspot.flags & 0x80) == 0x80)) {
        alfred_facing_direction = 2;  // Face DOWN
    }
    else {
        alfred_facing_direction = 3;  // Face UP
    }
}
```

**The algorithm:**
1. **First priority: Horizontal separation** - If Alfred and the target don't overlap horizontally, face left or right based on which side the target is on
2. **Second priority: Vertical positioning** - If horizontally overlapping, check vertical relationship and face up or down
3. **Takes into account Alfred's sprite dimensions** - Uses his width, height, and scale factors, not just his position point
4. **Different logic for sprites vs hotspots** - Sprites have Z-depth checks, hotspots have flag checks

This is significantly more sophisticated than the simple X/Y comparison shown in the documentation!

<tool-use data-tool-type="task" data-tool-name="manage_todo_list">
<details>
<summary>Tool use: **manage_todo_list** • Using "Manage and track todo items for task planning"</summary>

**Starting: *Document save game state structure* (4/4)**

- [x] Find save game functions
  > Found state arrays and room data offsets. The game stores state at fixed memory locations that get written to save files.
- [x] Analyze room 0 hotspot handlers
  > The handlers are in dispatch tables loaded from ALFRED.X files at runtime, not in the EXE itself
- [x] Analyze room 14 walkbox modification
  > Walkboxes are at room_sprite_data_ptr + 0x218, count at +0x213. Dynamic additions are saved in the save file.
- [-] Document save game state structure
  > Documenting findings based on confirmed analysis

</details>
</tool-use>

---

The user wants me to analyze the saving system in a game using Ghidra. They're particularly interested in:
1. How room metadata is saved (walkboxes, stickers, hotspots, exits)
2. How the game tracks which stickers are on
3. Which conversations have been gone through
4. Which hotspots are enabled/disabled
5. Which exits are enabled
6. Which walkboxes to add/remove

Let me start by exploring the Ghidra project to understand the codebase. I should look for:
- Save/load functions
- Functions related to walkboxes, hotspots, stickers

| +0x1BF+ | Exit array (14 bytes each) - **exit enabled flag at +0x02 within each entry** |

| +0x47A | Hotspot count |
| +0x47B+ | Hotspot array (9 bytes each) |

### 3. **Sprite/Sticker Visibility (CONFIRMED)**

- `0xFF` = sprite disabled/invisible
- `0x00-0xFE` = active Z-depth layer

### 4. **Exit Enable/Disable (CONFIRMED)**

Exit enabled flag is at: `room_sprite_data_ptr + 0x1BF + (exit_id × 0x0E) + 0x02`

- Value `1` = exit enabled

## CONFIRMED: Save Game State System Analysis

### Overview

The save game system in Alfred Pelrock works by **saving runtime game state** from fixed memory addresses. The game state is spread across several memory regions.

### 1. Global State Variables (Addresses confirmed from documentation and Ghidra)

| Runtime Address | Name | Size | Purpose |
|----------------|------|------|---------|
| `0x0004fb94` | `current_room_number` | 2 bytes | Current room ID |
| `0x0004fb96` | `alfred_x_position` | 2 bytes | Alfred's X coordinate |
| `0x0004fb98` | `alfred_y_position` | 2 bytes | Alfred's Y coordinate |
| `0x0004fba0` | `selected_inventory_item` | 2 bytes | Currently held item (-1 = none) |
| `0x0004fba4` | `conversation_branch_state_array` | 4×rooms bytes | Conversation choices per room |
| `0x0004fc94` | `inventory_item_ids` | ~32 bytes | Array of inventory item IDs |

### 2. Per-Room State (at `room_sprite_data_ptr`)

When you load a room, `room_sprite_data_ptr` points to the room's runtime data structure. Modifiable state includes:

| Offset | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `+0x05` | u8 | Sprite count |
| `+0x1BE` | u8 | Exit count |
| `+0x1BF + exit×14 + 2` | u8 | Exit N enabled (0=disabled, 1=enabled) |
| `+0x213` | u8 | Walkbox count |
| `+0x218 + walkbox×9` | 9 bytes | Walkbox N: x(2), y(2), w(2), h(2), flags(1) |
| `+0x47A` | u8 | Hotspot count |
| `+0x47B + hotspot×9` | 9 bytes | Hotspot data |

### 3. Sprite/Sticker Visibility

Each sprite has a 44-byte (0x2C) structure. The **Z-depth** at offset `+0x21` controls visibility:
- `0xFF` = invisible/disabled
- `0x00-0xFE` = visible with that Z-order

**To enable a sticker:** Set `room_sprite_data_ptr + sprite×0x2C + 0x21` to a valid Z-value.
**To disable a sticker:** Set the same byte to `0xFF`.

### 4. Save File Layout (Based on user's data)

The save file appears to store:

1. **Header** - Basic game state
2. **Global variables** - Position, room, inventory
3. **Per-room delta state** - Changes from original room data:
   - Extra walkboxes added
   - Sticker enable/disable states
   - Exit enable states
   - Hotspot enable states (moved to 640×400 = disabled)

**User's observed data at 0x25F1:**
```
B4 01 64 01 04 00 0E 00 00   // Walkbox 2: x=436, y=356, w=4, h=14, flags=0
B8 01 70 01 94 00 02 00 00   // Walkbox 3: x=440, y=368, w=148, h=2, flags=0
```

### 5. How State Changes Work

The game uses **F8 action codes** in text data to trigger state changes. When text containing `F8 XX XX` is displayed:

1. Game reads the 2-byte action ID
2. Looks up ID in `F8_ACTION_DISPATCH_TABLE` at `0x00047e58`
3. Calls the corresponding function which:
   - Enables/disables exits
   - Shows/hides stickers (sets sprite Z-depth)
   - Adds walkboxes
   - Modifies hotspot positions

### 6. Hotspot Disable Pattern

For Room 0 drawer (extra ID 261):
- **Disabled hotspot** = X/Y moved to 640×400 (off-screen)
- The game doesn't delete hotspots, it relocates them off-screen

For Room 0 door (extra ID 268):
- Opens exit at `room_sprite_data_ptr + 0x1BF + exit_index×14 + 2` = 1
- Shows door-open sticker by setting sprite Z-depth ≠ 0xFF

### 7. Key Functions (from documentation cross-referenced with Ghidra)

| Function | Address | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `execute_hotspot_script_table` | 0x19041 | Dispatches hotspot actions by extra ID |
| `handle_dialog_interaction` | 0x18f10 | Handles F8 action codes during text |
| `update_conversation_state` | 0x1b666 | Updates conversation branch state |
| `render_scene` | various | Calls passing sprite dispatchers |
| `load_room_and_init_alfred` | 0x152f5 | Loads room data, builds text pointers |

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\nimport os\nimport sys\n\ndef analyze_save(path):\n    with open(path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f'File: {os.path.basename(path)}')\n    print(f'File size: {len(data)} bytes (0x{len(data):x})')\n    print()\n    \n    # Print header\n    print('=== First 512 bytes ===')\n    for i in range(0, min(512, len(data)), 16):\n        hex_part = ' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in data[i:i+16])\n        ascii_part = ''.join(chr(b) if 32 &lt;= b &lt; 127 else '.' for b in data[i:i+16])\n        print(f'{i:04x}: {hex_part:&lt;48} {ascii_part}')\n    \n    # Search for walkbox pattern\n    walkbox_pattern = bytes([0xB4, 0x01, 0x64, 0x01, 0x04, 0x00, 0x0E, 0x00, 0x00])\n    pos = data.find(walkbox_pattern)\n    if pos &gt;= 0:\n        print(f'\\n=== Found walkbox pattern at offset 0x{pos:04x} ({pos}) ===')\n        # Print context around it\n        start = max(0, pos - 32)\n        end = min(len(data), pos + 64)\n        print(f'Context (offset 0x{start:04x} to 0x{end:04x}):')\n        for i in range(start, end, 16):\n            hex_part = ' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in data[i:min(i+16, end)])\n            ascii_part = ''.join(chr(b) if 32 &lt;= b &lt; 127 else '.' for b in data[i:min(i+16, end)])\n            marker = ' &lt;-- WALKBOX' if i &lt;= pos &lt; i+16 else ''\n            print(f'{i:04x}: {hex_part:&lt;48} {ascii_part}{marker}')\n    else:\n        print('\\nWalkbox pattern NOT found in this save file')\n    \n    return data\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    saves_dir = '/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/saves'\n    \n    # Analyze first save\n    save_path = os.path.join(saves_dir, 'SALVAJOC.000')\n    if os.path.exists(save_path):\n        analyze_save(save_path)\n    \n    # Also check for the walkbox pattern in all saves\n    print('\\n\\n=== Checking all saves for walkbox pattern ===')\n    for fname in sorted(os.listdir(saves_dir)):\n        if fname.startswith('SALVAJOC'):\n            fpath = os.path.join(saves_dir, fname)\n            with open(fpath, 'rb') as f:\n                data = f.read()\n            walkbox_pattern = bytes([0xB4, 0x01, 0x64, 0x01, 0x04, 0x00, 0x0E, 0x00, 0x00])\n            pos = data.find(walkbox_pattern)\n            if pos &gt;= 0:\n                print(f'{fname}: FOUND at offset 0x{pos:04x} ({pos})')\n            else:\n                print(f'{fname}: not found')\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze SALVAJOC save game files for Alfred Pelrock game.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport glob\n\nSAVES_DIR = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/saves\"\nWALKBOX_PATTERN = bytes([0xB4, 0x01, 0x64, 0x01, 0x04, 0x00, 0x0E, 0x00, 0x00, \n                         0xB8, 0x01, 0x70, 0x01, 0x94, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0x00])\n\ndef hex_dump(data, bytes_per_line=16, offset=0):\n    \"\"\"Generate a hex dump of binary data.\"\"\"\n    lines = []\n    for i in range(0, len(data), bytes_per_line):\n        chunk = data[i:i+bytes_per_line]\n        hex_part = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in chunk)\n        ascii_part = ''.join(chr(b) if 32 &lt;= b &lt; 127 else '.' for b in chunk)\n        lines.append(f'{offset+i:08X}  {hex_part:&lt;{bytes_per_line*3}}  {ascii_part}')\n    return '\\n'.join(lines)\n\ndef find_pattern(data, pattern):\n    \"\"\"Find all occurrences of a pattern in data.\"\"\"\n    offsets = []\n    start = 0\n    while True:\n        pos = data.find(pattern, start)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        offsets.append(pos)\n        start = pos + 1\n    return offsets\n\ndef analyze_structure(data, filename):\n    \"\"\"Try to identify structure in the save file.\"\"\"\n    info = []\n    \n    # Check for potential room number (typically 0-55 for this game)\n    # Look at first few bytes for potential header\n    if len(data) &gt;= 4:\n        # Try little-endian 16-bit values\n        val0 = int.from_bytes(data[0:2], 'little')\n        val1 = int.from_bytes(data[2:4], 'little')\n        info.append(f\"  First 2 bytes as uint16 LE: {val0} (0x{val0:04X})\")\n        info.append(f\"  Bytes 2-4 as uint16 LE: {val1} (0x{val1:04X})\")\n    \n    if len(data) &gt;= 8:\n        # Check for coordinates (typically 0-320 for x, 0-200 for y)\n        for i in range(0, min(32, len(data)-1), 2):\n            val = int.from_bytes(data[i:i+2], 'little')\n            if 0 &lt; val &lt; 320:\n                info.append(f\"  Offset {i}: {val} (possible X coord)\")\n            elif 0 &lt; val &lt; 200:\n                info.append(f\"  Offset {i}: {val} (possible Y coord)\")\n    \n    # Look for room numbers in the file\n    for i in range(min(64, len(data))):\n        if data[i] &lt;= 55 and data[i] &gt; 0:\n            # Could be a room number\n            pass  # Don't spam with all possible room numbers\n    \n    return info\n\ndef main():\n    # Get all save files\n    save_files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(SAVES_DIR, \"SALVAJOC.*\")))\n    \n    print(\"=\" * 80)\n    print(\"SALVAJOC SAVE FILE ANALYSIS\")\n    print(\"=\" * 80)\n    \n    # 1. File sizes\n    print(\"\\n### FILE SIZES ###\\n\")\n    file_data = {}\n    for f in save_files:\n        size = os.path.getsize(f)\n        basename = os.path.basename(f)\n        file_data[f] = {'size': size, 'basename': basename}\n        print(f\"{basename}: {size:,} bytes (0x{size:X})\")\n    \n    # Group by size\n    print(\"\\n### FILES GROUPED BY SIZE ###\\n\")\n    sizes = {}\n    for f, info in file_data.items():\n        sz = info['size']\n        if sz not in sizes:\n            sizes[sz] = []\n        sizes[sz].append(info['basename'])\n    for sz in sorted(sizes.keys()):\n        print(f\"{sz:,} bytes: {', '.join(sizes[sz])}\")\n    \n    # 2. Hex dump of first 256 bytes of SALVAJOC.000 and SALVAJOC.020\n    print(\"\\n### HEX DUMP - SALVAJOC.000 (first 256 bytes) ###\\n\")\n    save000 = os.path.join(SAVES_DIR, \"SALVAJOC.000\")\n    if os.path.exists(save000):\n        with open(save000, 'rb') as f:\n            data = f.read()\n            file_data[save000]['data'] = data\n            print(hex_dump(data[:256]))\n    \n    print(\"\\n### HEX DUMP - SALVAJOC.020 (first 256 bytes) ###\\n\")\n    save020 = os.path.join(SAVES_DIR, \"SALVAJOC.020\")\n    if os.path.exists(save020):\n        with open(save020, 'rb') as f:\n            data = f.read()\n            file_data[save020]['data'] = data\n            print(hex_dump(data[:256]))\n    \n    # 3. Search for walkbox pattern\n    print(\"\\n### WALKBOX PATTERN SEARCH ###\")\n    print(f\"Pattern: {' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in WALKBOX_PATTERN)}\")\n    print(f\"Pattern length: {len(WALKBOX_PATTERN)} bytes\\n\")\n    \n    found_in = []\n    for f in save_files:\n        with open(f, 'rb') as fp:\n            data = fp.read()\n        offsets = find_pattern(data, WALKBOX_PATTERN)\n        if offsets:\n            basename = os.path.basename(f)\n            found_in.append((basename, offsets))\n            print(f\"{basename}: FOUND at offset(s) {', '.join(f'0x{o:X} ({o})' for o in offsets)}\")\n    \n    if not found_in:\n        print(\"Pattern NOT FOUND in any save file.\")\n        \n        # Let's search for partial matches\n        print(\"\\nSearching for partial pattern (first 9 bytes)...\")\n        partial = WALKBOX_PATTERN[:9]\n        for f in save_files:\n            with open(f, 'rb') as fp:\n                data = fp.read()\n            offsets = find_pattern(data, partial)\n            if offsets:\n                basename = os.path.basename(f)\n                print(f\"{basename}: Partial match at offset(s) {', '.join(f'0x{o:X}' for o in offsets)}\")\n    \n    # 4. Structure analysis\n    print(\"\\n### STRUCTURE ANALYSIS ###\\n\")\n    \n    # Compare first bytes of multiple files\n    print(\"First 32 bytes comparison across save files:\")\n    for f in save_files[:5]:  # First 5 files\n        with open(f, 'rb') as fp:\n            data = fp.read(32)\n        basename = os.path.basename(f)\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in data)\n        print(f\"{basename}: {hex_str}\")\n    \n    # Look for common values\n    print(\"\\n\\nLooking for potential room numbers and coordinates in SALVAJOC.000...\")\n    if os.path.exists(save000):\n        with open(save000, 'rb') as f:\n            data = f.read()\n        \n        # First 64 bytes interpreted as 16-bit LE values\n        print(\"\\nFirst 64 bytes as 16-bit LE values:\")\n        for i in range(0, 64, 2):\n            val = int.from_bytes(data[i:i+2], 'little')\n            annotation = \"\"\n            if val &lt;= 55:\n                annotation = \" (possible room #)\"\n            elif 100 &lt;= val &lt;= 319:\n                annotation = \" (possible X coord)\"\n            elif val &lt;= 199:\n                annotation = \" (possible Y coord)\"\n            print(f\"  Offset 0x{i:02X}: {val:5d} (0x{val:04X}){annotation}\")\n    \n    # Compare different save files at specific offsets\n    print(\"\\n\\nComparing byte values at specific offsets across all saves:\")\n    print(\"(Looking for room numbers, player position, etc.)\\n\")\n    \n    all_data = {}\n    for f in save_files:\n        with open(f, 'rb') as fp:\n            all_data[os.path.basename(f)] = fp.read()\n    \n    # Check offset 0 (often contains version or type)\n    print(\"Offset 0x00 (first byte):\")\n    for name, data in sorted(all_data.items()):\n        if data:\n            print(f\"  {name}: {data[0]:3d} (0x{data[0]:02X})\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nDetailed structure analysis of SALVAJOC save game files.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport glob\nimport struct\n\nSAVES_DIR = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/saves\"\n\ndef analyze_header(data):\n    \"\"\"Analyze the save file header structure.\"\"\"\n    print(\"=\" * 60)\n    print(\"HEADER STRUCTURE ANALYSIS\")\n    print(\"=\" * 60)\n    \n    # Bytes 0x00-0x0F: Magic/signature \"Tic-Tac-Toe 1995\"\n    magic = data[0:16].decode('ascii', errors='replace')\n    print(f\"0x00-0x0F: Magic signature: '{magic}'\")\n    \n    # Bytes 0x10-0x25: Room/save name (null-terminated, padded with spaces)\n    room_name = data[0x10:0x26].rstrip(b'\\x00\\x20').decode('ascii', errors='replace')\n    print(f\"0x10-0x25: Save name: '{room_name}'\")\n    \n    # Now analyze the game state data starting at 0x26\n    print(f\"\\n0x26: Room number byte: {data[0x26]} (0x{data[0x26]:02X})\")\n    \n    # Coordinates seem to be at specific offsets\n    # Let's read them as 16-bit little-endian\n    print(f\"\\nGame state data (starting at 0x26):\")\n    \n    val_26 = struct.unpack_from('&lt;H', data, 0x26)[0]\n    val_28 = struct.unpack_from('&lt;H', data, 0x28)[0]\n    val_2a = struct.unpack_from('&lt;H', data, 0x2A)[0]\n    val_2c = struct.unpack_from('&lt;H', data, 0x2C)[0]\n    val_2e = struct.unpack_from('&lt;H', data, 0x2E)[0]\n    val_30 = struct.unpack_from('&lt;H', data, 0x30)[0]\n    val_32 = struct.unpack_from('&lt;H', data, 0x32)[0]\n    \n    print(f\"  0x26-0x27: {val_26:5} (0x{val_26:04X}) - likely contains room # in low byte ({data[0x26]})\")\n    print(f\"  0x28-0x29: {val_28:5} (0x{val_28:04X}) - possible X coordinate?\")\n    print(f\"  0x2A-0x2B: {val_2a:5} (0x{val_2a:04X}) - possible Y or target X?\")\n    print(f\"  0x2C-0x2D: {val_2c:5} (0x{val_2c:04X})\")\n    print(f\"  0x2E-0x2F: {val_2e:5} (0x{val_2e:04X})\")\n    print(f\"  0x30-0x31: {val_30:5} (0x{val_30:04X})\")\n    print(f\"  0x32-0x33: {val_32:5} (0x{val_32:04X})\")\n    \n    return data[0x26]  # Return room number byte\n\ndef compare_saves():\n    \"\"\"Compare specific offsets across all save files.\"\"\"\n    save_files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(SAVES_DIR, \"SALVAJOC.*\")))\n    \n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\" * 80)\n    print(\"COMPARING KEY OFFSETS ACROSS SAVE FILES\")\n    print(\"=\" * 80)\n    \n    print(\"\\n{:&lt;15} {:&gt;10} {:&gt;12} {:&gt;8} {:&gt;8} {:&gt;8} {:&gt;8}\".format(\n        \"File\", \"Size\", \"SaveName\", \"Rm#\", \"0x28\", \"0x2A\", \"0x2E\"))\n    print(\"-\" * 80)\n    \n    for f in save_files:\n        with open(f, 'rb') as fp:\n            data = fp.read()\n        \n        basename = os.path.basename(f)\n        size = len(data)\n        \n        # Extract save name\n        save_name = data[0x10:0x26].rstrip(b'\\x00\\x20').decode('ascii', errors='replace')[:10]\n        \n        # Room number at 0x26\n        room_num = data[0x26]\n        \n        # Coordinates\n        val_28 = struct.unpack_from('&lt;H', data, 0x28)[0]\n        val_2a = struct.unpack_from('&lt;H', data, 0x2A)[0]\n        val_2e = struct.unpack_from('&lt;H', data, 0x2E)[0]\n        \n        print(f\"{basename:&lt;15} {size:&gt;10,} {save_name:&gt;12} {room_num:&gt;8} {val_28:&gt;8} {val_2a:&gt;8} {val_2e:&gt;8}\")\n\ndef find_inventory_section(data):\n    \"\"\"Try to identify inventory section in save file.\"\"\"\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\" * 60)\n    print(\"SEARCHING FOR INVENTORY/FLAGS SECTION\")\n    print(\"=\" * 60)\n    \n    # Look at bytes 0x34-0x100 which seem to have flags\n    print(\"\\nBytes 0x34-0x6F (potential game flags/inventory):\")\n    \n    # Count non-zero bytes in different sections\n    sections = [\n        (0x34, 0x50, \"Section 0x34-0x4F\"),\n        (0x50, 0x70, \"Section 0x50-0x6F\"),\n        (0x70, 0x90, \"Section 0x70-0x8F\"),\n        (0x90, 0xB0, \"Section 0x90-0xAF\"),\n        (0xB0, 0xD0, \"Section 0xB0-0xCF\"),\n        (0xD0, 0xF0, \"Section 0xD0-0xEF\"),\n    ]\n    \n    for start, end, name in sections:\n        section = data[start:end]\n        non_zero = sum(1 for b in section if b != 0)\n        print(f\"  {name}: {non_zero} non-zero bytes\")\n        if non_zero &gt; 0 and non_zero &lt; 20:\n            # Show the non-zero bytes\n            for i, b in enumerate(section):\n                if b != 0:\n                    print(f\"    Offset 0x{start+i:02X}: {b} (0x{b:02X})\")\n\ndef analyze_walkbox_context(data, pattern_offset):\n    \"\"\"Analyze the context around the walkbox pattern.\"\"\"\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\" * 60)\n    print(f\"WALKBOX PATTERN CONTEXT (at offset 0x{pattern_offset:X})\")\n    print(\"=\" * 60)\n    \n    # Show 32 bytes before\n    start = max(0, pattern_offset - 32)\n    print(f\"\\n32 bytes BEFORE pattern (0x{start:X} - 0x{pattern_offset:X}):\")\n    for i in range(start, pattern_offset, 16):\n        chunk = data[i:i+16]\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in chunk)\n        ascii_str = ''.join(chr(b) if 32 &lt;= b &lt; 127 else '.' for b in chunk)\n        print(f\"  {i:08X}  {hex_str}  {ascii_str}\")\n    \n    # Show the pattern and 48 bytes after\n    print(f\"\\nPattern and 48 bytes AFTER (0x{pattern_offset:X}):\")\n    for i in range(pattern_offset, min(len(data), pattern_offset + 64), 16):\n        chunk = data[i:i+16]\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in chunk)\n        ascii_str = ''.join(chr(b) if 32 &lt;= b &lt; 127 else '.' for b in chunk)\n        print(f\"  {i:08X}  {hex_str}  {ascii_str}\")\n\ndef main():\n    # Analyze SALVAJOC.000 in detail\n    save000 = os.path.join(SAVES_DIR, \"SALVAJOC.000\")\n    with open(save000, 'rb') as f:\n        data000 = f.read()\n    \n    print(\"Analyzing SALVAJOC.000 (size: {} bytes)\\n\".format(len(data000)))\n    \n    room_num = analyze_header(data000)\n    find_inventory_section(data000)\n    \n    # Find walkbox pattern\n    WALKBOX_PATTERN = bytes([0xB4, 0x01, 0x64, 0x01, 0x04, 0x00, 0x0E, 0x00, 0x00, \n                             0xB8, 0x01, 0x70, 0x01, 0x94, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0x00])\n    offset = data000.find(WALKBOX_PATTERN)\n    if offset &gt;= 0:\n        analyze_walkbox_context(data000, offset)\n    \n    # Compare all saves\n    compare_saves()\n    \n    # Now analyze SALVAJOC.020 for comparison\n    print(\"\\n\\n\" + \"=\" * 80)\n    print(\"SALVAJOC.020 ANALYSIS (for comparison)\")\n    print(\"=\" * 80)\n    \n    save020 = os.path.join(SAVES_DIR, \"SALVAJOC.020\")\n    with open(save020, 'rb') as f:\n        data020 = f.read()\n    \n    analyze_header(data020)\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

}

  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/deep_analyze_saves.py)",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nDeep analysis of Alfred Pelrock save files to understand structure.\n\"\"\"\nimport os\nimport struct\n\nSAVE_DIR = '/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/saves'\n\ndef read_save(path):\n    with open(path, 'rb') as f:\n        return f.read()\n\ndef analyze_header(data):\n    \"\"\"Analyze the header section of the save file.\"\"\"\n    print(\"=== Header Analysis (First 64 bytes) ===\")\n    \n    # Magic header \"Tic-Tac-Toe 1995\"\n    magic = data[0:16].rstrip(b'\\x00').decode('ascii', errors='replace')\n    print(f\"Magic (0x00-0x0F): '{magic}'\")\n    \n    # Next bytes\n    print(f\"Bytes 0x10-0x1F: {data[0x10:0x20].hex(' ')}\")\n    print(f\"Bytes 0x20-0x2F: {data[0x20:0x30].hex(' ')}\")\n    print(f\"Bytes 0x30-0x3F: {data[0x30:0x40].hex(' ')}\")\n    \n    # Specific fields\n    if len(data) &gt; 0x28:\n        room = data[0x26]\n        player_x = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[0x28:0x2A])[0]\n        player_y = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[0x2A:0x2C])[0]\n        print(f\"\\nRoom number (0x26): {room}\")\n        print(f\"Player X (0x28): {player_x}\")\n        print(f\"Player Y (0x2A): {player_y}\")\n\ndef find_patterns(data, description):\n    \"\"\"Find specific patterns in the data.\"\"\"\n    # Walkbox pattern from room 14\n    walkbox_pattern = bytes([0xB4, 0x01, 0x64, 0x01, 0x04, 0x00, 0x0E, 0x00, 0x00])\n    pos = data.find(walkbox_pattern)\n    if pos &gt;= 0:\n        print(f\"Walkbox pattern found at 0x{pos:04x}\")\n        return pos\n    return -1\n\ndef compare_saves(save1_path, save2_path):\n    \"\"\"Compare two save files and show differences.\"\"\"\n    data1 = read_save(save1_path)\n    data2 = read_save(save2_path)\n    \n    print(f\"\\n=== Comparing {os.path.basename(save1_path)} vs {os.path.basename(save2_path)} ===\")\n    print(f\"Size: {len(data1)} vs {len(data2)} bytes\")\n    \n    # Find first difference\n    min_len = min(len(data1), len(data2))\n    diff_count = 0\n    first_diff = -1\n    diff_regions = []\n    region_start = -1\n    \n    for i in range(min_len):\n        if data1[i] != data2[i]:\n            if first_diff == -1:\n                first_diff = i\n            if region_start == -1:\n                region_start = i\n            diff_count += 1\n        else:\n            if region_start != -1:\n                diff_regions.append((region_start, i))\n                region_start = -1\n    \n    if region_start != -1:\n        diff_regions.append((region_start, min_len))\n    \n    print(f\"Total different bytes: {diff_count}\")\n    print(f\"First difference at: 0x{first_diff:04x}\" if first_diff &gt;= 0 else \"Files are identical in overlapping region\")\n    \n    if diff_regions:\n        print(f\"\\nDifference regions (first 20):\")\n        for start, end in diff_regions[:20]:\n            length = end - start\n            print(f\"  0x{start:04x}-0x{end-1:04x} ({length} bytes)\")\n            if length &lt;= 16:\n                print(f\"    File 1: {data1[start:end].hex(' ')}\")\n                print(f\"    File 2: {data2[start:end].hex(' ')}\")\n\ndef analyze_structure(data, fname):\n    \"\"\"Attempt to identify structure within the save file.\"\"\"\n    print(f\"\\n=== Analyzing {fname} (size {len(data)} bytes) ===\")\n    \n    analyze_header(data)\n    \n    # Look for repeated patterns (9-byte structures like walkboxes)\n    print(\"\\n=== Searching for structures ===\")\n    \n    # Search for potential array regions (many consecutive similar-sized entries)\n    # Walkboxes are 9 bytes: x(2), y(2), w(2), h(2), flags(1)\n    \n    walkbox_pos = find_patterns(data, fname)\n    \n    # Look for potential state flag arrays (groups of bytes that are 0 or 1)\n    print(\"\\n=== Potential State Arrays ===\")\n    for offset in range(0x100, min(0x1000, len(data)), 0x100):\n        region = data[offset:offset+64]\n        ones_and_zeros = sum(1 for b in region if b in (0, 1))\n        if ones_and_zeros &gt; 50:\n            print(f\"  0x{offset:04x}: {ones_and_zeros}/64 bytes are 0 or 1\")\n            print(f\"    Sample: {region[:32].hex(' ')}\")\n\ndef main():\n    saves = []\n    for fname in sorted(os.listdir(SAVE_DIR)):\n        if fname.startswith('SALVAJOC'):\n            path = os.path.join(SAVE_DIR, fname)\n            data = read_save(path)\n            room = data[0x26] if len(data) &gt; 0x26 else -1\n            saves.append((fname, path, data, room))\n            print(f\"{fname}: {len(data):6} bytes, room {room:2d}\")\n    \n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*60)\n    \n    # Analyze first save in detail\n    if saves:\n        analyze_structure(saves[0][2], saves[0][0])\n    \n    # Compare saves from different rooms\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*60)\n    \n    # Find two saves from different rooms\n    room0_save = None\n    room14_save = None\n    for fname, path, data, room in saves:\n        if room == 0 and room0_save is None:\n            room0_save = (fname, path, data)\n        elif room == 14 and room14_save is None:\n            room14_save = (fname, path, data)\n    \n    if room0_save and room14_save:\n        compare_saves(room0_save[1], room14_save[1])\n    \n    # Show offset 0x25F1 region in all saves\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*60)\n    print(\"=== Offset 0x25F1 region in all saves (walkbox location) ===\")\n    for fname, path, data, room in saves:\n        if len(data) &gt; 0x2610:\n            region = data[0x25F1:0x2610]\n            # Check if this looks like walkbox data (reasonable x/y values)\n            x = struct.unpack('&lt;H', region[0:2])[0] if len(region) &gt;= 2 else 0\n            y = struct.unpack('&lt;H', region[2:4])[0] if len(region) &gt;= 4 else 0\n            has_data = x &lt; 640 and y &lt; 400 and x &gt; 0  # Reasonable screen coords\n            marker = \"WALKBOX\" if has_data else \"\"\n            print(f\"{fname} (room {room:2d}): {region[:18].hex(' ')} {marker}\")\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/SAVE_GAME_SYSTEM_ANALYSIS.md)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/SAVE_GAME_SYSTEM_ANALYSIS.md)",
  "isConfirmed": {

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "# Alfred Pelrock Save Game System Analysis\n\n## Save File Structure\n\n### File Location\n- Path: &#96;SALVAJOC.XXX&#96; where XXX is 000-999 (save slot number)\n- Files typically range from 9KB to 11.5KB depending on game progress\n\n### Binary Structure\n\n| Offset | Size | Description | Notes |\n|--------|------|-------------|-------|\n| 0x00-0x0F | 16 | Magic Header | ASCII \"Tic-Tac-Toe 1995\" |\n| 0x10-0x25 | 22 | Save Name | User-defined, space-padded |\n| 0x26 | 1 | Room Number | Current room (0-55) |\n| 0x27 | 1 | Unknown | Usually 0x00 |\n| 0x28-0x29 | 2 | Player X | Little-endian uint16 |\n| 0x2A-0x2B | 2 | Player Y | Little-endian uint16 |\n| 0x2C-0x33 | 8 | Unknown | Position-related? |\n| 0x34-0xFF | ~204 | Game Flags | Sparse flag arrays |\n| 0x100-0x25F0 | ~9KB | Game State | Core state data |\n| 0x25F1+ | Variable | Walkbox Data | 9 bytes per walkbox |\n| Variable | Variable | Additional State | Depends on progress |\n\n### Walkbox Structure (9 bytes each, at offset 0x25F1)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;c\nstruct Walkbox {\n    uint16_t x;      // +0: X position\n    uint16_t y;      // +2: Y position  \n    uint16_t width;  // +4: Width\n    uint16_t height; // +6: Height\n    uint8_t flags;   // +8: Flags/type (usually 0)\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nExample from Room 14:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nWalkbox 1: x=436, y=356, w=4,   h=14, flags=0  (B4 01 64 01 04 00 0E 00 00)\nWalkbox 2: x=440, y=368, w=148, h=2,  flags=0  (B8 01 70 01 94 00 02 00 00)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## In-Game State Variables\n\n### Core Memory Addresses (Virtual)\n\n| Address | Name | Description |\n|---------|------|-------------|\n| 0x0004fb94 | current_room_number | Current room ID (byte) |\n| 0x0004fba4 | conversation_branch_state_array | Conversation states (room*4 + slot) |\n| 0x0004fc94 | inventory_item_ids | Array of item IDs in inventory |\n| 0x0004fba0 | current_selected_item | Currently held inventory item (-1 if none) |\n| 0x00038e38 | game_mode_or_chapter | Current chapter/game mode |\n\n### Room Data Structure (in memory at room_sprite_data_ptr)\n\n| Offset | Size | Description |\n|--------|------|-------------|\n| +0x05 | 1 | Sprite count |\n| +0x06 | 44 each | Sprite headers |\n| +0x1BE | 1 | Exit count |\n| +0x1BF | 14 each | Exit array |\n| +0x213 | 1 | Walkbox count |\n| +0x218 | 9 each | Walkbox array |\n| +0x47A | 1 | Hotspot count |\n| +0x47C | 9 each | Hotspot array |\n| +0x3DA | varies | Text pointer table |\n\n## State That Needs Saving/Loading\n\n### 1. Conversation States\n- **Array**: &#96;conversation_branch_state_array&#96; at 0x0004fba4\n- **Format**: &#96;array[room_number * 4 + branch_slot]&#96;\n- **Purpose**: Tracks which conversation branches have been taken\n- **Usage**: When value != 0, skip to alternate text branch\n\n### 2. Hotspot Enable/Disable\n- **Location**: &#96;room_sprite_data_ptr + 0x47C + hotspot_id * 9 + 1&#96;\n- **Flag**: action_flags byte, high bit indicates enabled state\n- **Triggered by**: F8 action codes in text data\n\n### 3. Exit Enable/Disable\n- **Location**: &#96;room_sprite_data_ptr + 0x1BF + exit_id * 14 + 2&#96;\n- **Flag**: Byte at offset +0x02 in exit structure (0 = disabled, non-0 = enabled)\n\n### 4. Walkbox Modifications (CRITICAL)\n- **Count**: &#96;room_sprite_data_ptr + 0x213&#96;\n- **Data**: &#96;room_sprite_data_ptr + 0x218&#96; (9 bytes each)\n- **Room 14 Example**: Opens new walkboxes after certain actions\n- **Save offset**: Fixed at 0x25F1 in save file\n\n### 5. Sprite/Sticker Visibility\n- **Pegatinas (stickers)**: Overlay sprites that can be shown/hidden\n- **Triggered by**: Hotspot actions via dispatch table at 0x47bf0\n- **Example**: Drawer in Room 0 (extra 261) places sticker #91\n\n### 6. Inventory\n- **Array**: &#96;inventory_item_ids&#96; at 0x0004fc94\n- **Format**: Array of uint16 item IDs\n- **Navigation**: 4 visible slots with scroll arrows\n\n## Key Dispatch Tables\n\n| Address | Purpose | Entry Size |\n|---------|---------|------------|\n| 0x00047bf0 | Hotspot action dispatch | 6 bytes (id:2 + func:4) |\n| 0x00047e58 | F8 action dispatch | 6 bytes (id:2 + func:4) |\n| 0x00048118 | Item combination table | Variable |\n| 0x000484e4 | Room initialization | 6 bytes (room:2 + func:4) |\n| 0x00048630 | Passing sprites (render_scene) | 6 bytes (room:2 + func:4) |\n| 0x000486a4 | Palette cycling | 6 bytes (room:2 + config:4) |\n| 0x000486fe | Menu slot actions | Variable |\n\n## How State Changes Are Triggered\n\n### F8 Action Codes\nFound in text data, format: &#96;F8 [id_low] [id_high]&#96;\n- Executed during text display/conversation\n- Looks up action ID in F8_ACTION_DISPATCH_TABLE\n- Actions include: enable/disable exits, show/hide stickers, update conversation state\n\n### Hotspot Actions\n- Player clicks hotspot → reads extra field (2 bytes at +0x06)\n- Looks up in hotspot_action_dispatch_table at 0x47bf0\n- Calls associated function to execute action\n\n## ScummVM Implementation Notes\n\n### Save/Load Functions to Implement\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;cpp\nclass AlfredSaveManager {\n    // Header\n    static const char MAGIC[] = \"Tic-Tac-Toe 1995\";\n    \n    struct SaveHeader {\n        char magic[16];\n        char saveName[22];\n        uint8 roomNumber;\n        uint8 padding;\n        uint16 playerX;\n        uint16 playerY;\n        // Additional fields...\n    };\n    \n    // State arrays to save\n    uint8 conversationStates[56 * 4];  // 224 bytes, one per room*4 slots\n    uint16 inventoryItems[MAX_INVENTORY];\n    \n    // Per-room state\n    struct RoomState {\n        uint8 exitEnabled[MAX_EXITS];      // From offset 0x1BF + n*14 + 2\n        uint8 hotspotEnabled[MAX_HOTSPOTS]; // From offset 0x47C + n*9 + 1\n        uint8 walkboxCount;                 // From offset 0x213\n        Walkbox walkboxes[MAX_WALKBOXES];   // From offset 0x218\n        // Sticker visibility flags\n    };\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Key Questions for Implementation\n\n1. **Walkbox Persistence**: Are modified walkboxes saved per-room or globally?\n   - Analysis shows: Fixed offset 0x25F1 suggests global storage\n   \n2. **State Size**: Why does file size vary (9KB-11.5KB)?\n   - Likely: Additional progress-dependent data appended\n   \n3. **Magic String Location**: Where is \"Tic-Tac-Toe 1995\" stored?\n   - Not in executable strings - likely in resource file or hardcoded in save function\n\n4. **Save Slot UI**: How are slots selected?\n   - Button coordinates: Save (132, 186, 81x34), Load (133, 222, 80x33)\n   - Menu handler at ~0x12918 (needs verification)\n\n## Files Involved\n\n| File | Purpose |\n|------|---------|\n| JUEGO.EXE (alfred.x) | Main executable with all logic |\n| SALVAJOC.XXX | Save game files |\n| ALFRED.1-B | Resource files (room data, graphics) |\n| PATH.DAT | Path configuration |\n\n## Next Steps for Complete Analysis\n\n1. Find the actual save/load functions by:\n   - Tracing file write operations\n   - Finding sprintf call that builds \"SALVAJOC.%03d\"\n   \n2. Determine exact state array sizes and offsets\n\n3. Map which F8 actions modify which state\n\n4. Verify walkbox modification mechanism in Room 14\n\n5. Test save/load cycle to confirm all state is preserved\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

- **Game Flags**: Offset 0x34-0xFF (~204 bytes of sparse flags)
- **Core State**: Offset 0x100-0x25F0 (~9KB)
- **Walkboxes**: Fixed offset 0x25F1 (9 bytes each: x/y/w/h as uint16 + 1 byte flags)

### Key Memory Addresses
| Address | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| 0x0004fb94 | Current room number |
| 0x0004fba4 | Conversation branch state array (room*4 + slot) |
| 0x0004fc94 | Inventory item IDs |

| 0x00038e38 | Game mode/chapter |

| +0x218 | Walkbox array start |
| +0x47A | Hotspot count |
| +0x47C | Hotspot array start |
| +0x1BE | Exit count |
| +0x1BF | Exit array start |

F8 means "trigger action" and 1101 is 273. So triggering action number 273 should add those walkboxes. I want to know where these walkboxes are retrieved or if they are hardcoded.

Ultimately what i need to figure out is how to save the game state in my scummvm implementation, so i want to mimic what the game is doing for this. Is it storing the entire list of hotspots, exits, walkboxes, conversations, per room? or only some sort of "diff".

I have verified that when you load a game the ALFRED.1 file (which contains rooms and their metadata) *does* change so saves effectively modify this file in runtime.

However when you start the game, you're taking to a clean slate so there must be a file somewhere storing the default values. My best guess is that this is ALFRED.8 but I have no proof.

Please verify all this for me.

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\nimport struct\n\nexe_path = '/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/JUEGO.EXE'\noutput_path = '/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/dispatch_table_analysis.txt'\n\ndata = open(exe_path, 'rb').read()\n\n# From Ghidra segments:\n# .object1 (code): 0x10000 - 0x24056 virtual\n# .object2 (data): 0x30000 - 0x39eaf virtual\n# .image: .image::00000000 - .image::00020485\n\n# The virtual address 0x47e58 is in the .image segment which starts at 0x40000 virtual\n# File offset calculation:\n# Need to find where .image segment starts in the file\n\n# Let's examine the PE/LE header to find section offsets\n# For a DOS/4G or DOS/4GW executable, we need to find the linear executable info\n\n# Let's search for F8 action entries directly\n# F8 actions have format: [uint16 action_id][uint32 func_ptr]\n# The terminator is typically 0xFFFF\n\nwith open(output_path, 'w') as f:\n    f.write(\"=== F8 Dispatch Table Search ===\\n\\n\")\n    \n    # Look for potential table starts by searching for entries with IDs in F8 range\n    # And followed by valid-looking function pointers (should be in code segment 0x10000-0x24000)\n    \n    # Let's search for the -1 terminator pattern (0xFFFF) that ends dispatch tables\n    f.write(\"Looking for dispatch table terminators (0xFFFF)...\\n\")\n    \n    # Search for 0xFFFF followed by looking backwards for table\n    terminators = []\n    pos = 0\n    while True:\n        pos = data.find(b'\\xff\\xff', pos)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        terminators.append(pos)\n        pos += 1\n    \n    f.write(f\"Found {len(terminators)} potential terminators\\n\\n\")\n    \n    # For each terminator, look backwards for a valid table\n    f.write(\"Analyzing potential F8 dispatch tables...\\n\")\n    \n    for term_pos in terminators:\n        # Go back and check if previous entries look like a dispatch table\n        # Each entry is 6 bytes\n        valid_entries = 0\n        check_pos = term_pos - 6\n        while check_pos &gt;= 0:\n            entry = data[check_pos:check_pos+6]\n            if len(entry) &lt; 6:\n                break\n            action_id = struct.unpack('&lt;H', entry[0:2])[0]\n            func_ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;I', entry[2:6])[0]\n            \n            # Valid entries have action IDs in reasonable range and func_ptr in code segment\n            if 0x100 &lt;= action_id &lt;= 0x300 and 0x10000 &lt;= func_ptr &lt;= 0x25000:\n                valid_entries += 1\n                check_pos -= 6\n            else:\n                break\n        \n        if valid_entries &gt;= 5:  # At least 5 valid entries\n            table_start = check_pos + 6\n            f.write(f\"\\n=== Potential table at file offset 0x{table_start:05x}, {valid_entries} entries ===\\n\")\n            \n            # Dump the table\n            for i in range(valid_entries + 1):  # +1 for terminator\n                entry_pos = table_start + i * 6\n                entry = data[entry_pos:entry_pos+6]\n                if len(entry) &gt;= 6:\n                    action_id = struct.unpack('&lt;H', entry[0:2])[0]\n                    func_ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;I', entry[2:6])[0]\n                    f.write(f\"  Entry {i}: offset=0x{entry_pos:05x} action_id=0x{action_id:04x} ({action_id}) func_ptr=0x{func_ptr:08x}\\n\")\n                    \n                    # Check if this is action 273 (0x111)\n                    if action_id == 0x111:\n                        f.write(f\"    *** FOUND ACTION 273 (0x111)! Function pointer: 0x{func_ptr:08x} ***\\n\")\n\nprint(f\"Analysis written to {output_path}\")\n",

}

# Reverse engineering game save system in Ghidra (2026-01-01 20:00Z)

_**User (2026-01-01 20:43Z)**_

i need to figure out how the saving system works, particularly for room metadata.

For instance in room 14 after some action two new walkboxes are added to the room. When i open a savegame with this action already executed, i can see the two walkboxes in ALFRED.1 and in the associated savegame (one at 436 * 356 with a width of 4 and a height of 14, the other one with a x,y of 440x 368 and w=148, h = 2, it looks like B4 01 64 01 04 00 0E 00 00 B8 01 70 01 94 00 02 00 00 in the savegame file). An example of a savegame with this info is SALVAJOC.006. A collection of saves is at files/saves/

In room 0 picking up certain objects moves their hotspot to 640x400, and places a "sticker" on top of the image below the hotspot. Also opening the door (extra value 268 in the hotspot struct) enables the only exit in this room, and places a "sticker" with the open door. Opening the drawer (extra 261 in the hotspot struct) disables its hotspot (i.e. moves it to 600x400) and places a sticker with the open drawer.

I want you to figure out on ghidra how this works. You can just try to figure out how the game stores which stickers are on, which conversations have been gone through (and disabled), which hotspots are enabled/disabled, which exits enabled, which walkboxes to add or remove.

per my inspection, the walkboxes in room 14 are triggered when talking to the salesman in the room ( the only NPC) after reading a certain book. At the end of this conversation in ALFRED.1 there is this sequence of bytes: F8 11 01. F8 means "trigger action" and 1101 is 273. So triggering action number 273 should add those walkboxes. I want to know where these walkboxes are retrived from or if they are hardcoded in the action trigger.

Ultimately what i need to figure out is how to save the game state in my scummvm implementation, so i want to mimic what the game is doing for this. Is it storing the entire list of hotspots, exits, walkboxes, stickers and conversations for each room? Or only some sort of "diff"?

I have verified that when you loade a game the ALFRED.1 file (which contains rooms and their metadata) does change so saves effectively modify this file in runtime.

However when you start the game you're taken to a clean slate so there must be a file somewhere storing the default values. My best guess is that this is ALFRED.8 but i have no proof, just a theory.

Please verify all this for me, rename functions and vars on ghidra as you go and remember heredoc inline python breaks my terminal if too long, and occasionally you cant read terminal output so keep that in mind and better work with scripts that output to a file.

Take all the time you need, but give me information you are CERTAIN about, not conjectures.

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze F8 action dispatch table at 0x47e58 in JUEGO.EXE\nLooking for action 273 (0x111) that adds walkboxes in room 14\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\n# JUEGO.EXE base offset when loaded (virtual address to file offset)\n# Virtual address 0x47e58, need to subtract image base\n# Based on DOS EXE, likely: file_offset = virtual - 0x10000 + header_size\n# Let's just search for the table pattern\n\ndef analyze_exe():\n    exe_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/JUEGO.EXE\"\n    \n    if not os.path.exists(exe_path):\n        print(f\"Cannot find {exe_path}\")\n        # Try alternate location\n        exe_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/JUEGO.EXE\"\n        if not os.path.exists(exe_path):\n            print(\"Cannot find JUEGO.EXE\")\n            return\n    \n    with open(exe_path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"EXE size: {len(data)} bytes\")\n    \n    # The dispatch table at 0x47e58 in Ghidra memory\n    # For DOS EXE, virtual address 0x47e58 corresponds to different file offset\n    # Usually: file_offset = virtual_addr - base_addr (often 0x10000)\n    # Let's calculate possible offsets\n    \n    base_candidates = [0, 0x10000, 0x1000]\n    \n    for base in base_candidates:\n        offset = 0x47e58 - base\n        if 0 &lt;= offset &lt; len(data):\n            print(f\"\\n=== Trying base 0x{base:x}, file offset 0x{offset:x} ===\")\n            \n            # Read some bytes and check if they look like a dispatch table\n            # Format: [u16 action_id] [u32 handler_address], repeating until 0xFFFF\n            pos = offset\n            entries = []\n            for i in range(100):  # Max 100 entries\n                if pos + 6 &gt; len(data):\n                    break\n                action_id = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n                handler = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n                \n                if action_id == 0xFFFF:\n                    print(f\"  Table terminator found at entry {i}\")\n                    break\n                    \n                entries.append((action_id, handler))\n                pos += 6\n                \n                # Print first few entries and action 273 if found\n                if i &lt; 5 or action_id == 273:\n                    print(f\"  Entry {i}: action_id=0x{action_id:04x} ({action_id}), handler=0x{handler:08x}\")\n            \n            # Check if we found action 273\n            for aid, handler in entries:\n                if aid == 273:\n                    print(f\"\\n*** FOUND ACTION 273! Handler at 0x{handler:08x} ***\")\n    \n    # Also search for the bytes F8 11 01 (trigger action 273)\n    print(\"\\n\\n=== Searching for F8 11 01 pattern in EXE ===\")\n    pattern = bytes([0xF8, 0x11, 0x01])\n    pos = 0\n    count = 0\n    while True:\n        pos = data.find(pattern, pos)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        print(f\"  Found at file offset 0x{pos:x}\")\n        count += 1\n        pos += 1\n    print(f\"Total occurrences: {count}\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    analyze_exe()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

{
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/analyze_dispatch_detailed.py)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/analyze_dispatch_detailed.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nRead F8 action dispatch table directly from Ghidra memory dump or by analyzing JUEGO.EXE\nwith correct offset calculations.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\ndef read_dispatch_table_from_exe():\n    \"\"\"\n    The dispatch table is at virtual address 0x47e58.\n    For Watcom DOS/4GW executables, we need to find the correct file offset.\n    \n    From Ghidra analysis:\n    - Table at 0x47e58 is referenced from 0x187eb in handle_conversation_tree\n    - Format: [u16 action_id][u32 handler_addr], 6 bytes each, terminated by 0xFFFF\n    \"\"\"\n    \n    exe_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/JUEGO.EXE\"\n    if not os.path.exists(exe_path):\n        print(f\"Cannot find {exe_path}\")\n        return\n    \n    with open(exe_path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"EXE size: {len(data)} bytes\")\n    \n    # DOS/4GW LE executable format\n    # First, find the DOS header and LE header\n    if data[:2] == b'MZ':\n        print(\"Found MZ header (DOS executable)\")\n        # Get pointer to LE header\n        le_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[0x3C:0x3E])[0]\n        print(f\"LE header offset: 0x{le_offset:x}\")\n        \n        if data[le_offset:le_offset+2] == b'LE':\n            print(\"Found LE header (Linear Executable)\")\n            \n            # Parse LE header to find object table and pages\n            # For our purposes, we can estimate the base address\n            # Virtual addresses in Ghidra typically start at a fixed base\n            \n            # Try to calculate correct offset\n            # Object base address is typically 0x10000 for DOS/4GW\n            # But we need to account for the object locations\n            \n    # Let's try a different approach - search for the reference pattern\n    # We know the dispatch loop is at 0x187eb and references 0x47e58\n    \n    # The pattern at 0x187eb should be:\n    # MOV BX, word ptr [EAX + 0x47e58]\n    # which encodes as: 66 8B 98 58 7E 04 00 (or similar)\n    \n    # Search for \"58 7E 04\" which is the address bytes of 0x47e58\n    target_patterns = [\n        bytes([0x58, 0x7E, 0x04, 0x00]),\n        bytes([0x58, 0x7E, 0x04])\n    ]\n    \n    print(\"\\n=== Searching for references to 0x47e58 ===\")\n    for pattern in target_patterns:\n        pos = 0\n        while True:\n            pos = data.find(pattern, pos)\n            if pos == -1:\n                break\n            # Show surrounding bytes\n            start = max(0, pos - 4)\n            end = min(len(data), pos + len(pattern) + 4)\n            print(f\"Found at 0x{pos:05x}: {data[start:end].hex()}\")\n            pos += 1\n    \n    # Now let's calculate the file offset for 0x47e58\n    # In DOS/4GW LE files, virtual addresses often have a fixed mapping\n    # Common patterns:\n    # - VA = file_offset + base (e.g., base = 0x10000)\n    # - Sections may have different bases\n    \n    print(\"\\n=== Trying to decode LE header ===\")\n    le_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[0x3C:0x3E])[0]\n    \n    # LE header fields\n    if data[le_offset:le_offset+2] == b'LE':\n        # Object table offset (from start of LE header)\n        obj_table_off = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[le_offset+0x40:le_offset+0x44])[0]\n        num_objects = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[le_offset+0x44:le_offset+0x48])[0]\n        \n        # Object page map offset\n        obj_pagemap_off = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[le_offset+0x48:le_offset+0x4C])[0]\n        \n        # Data pages offset \n        data_pages_off = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[le_offset+0x80:le_offset+0x84])[0]\n        \n        print(f\"Object table offset: 0x{obj_table_off:x}\")\n        print(f\"Number of objects: {num_objects}\")\n        print(f\"Data pages offset: 0x{data_pages_off:x}\")\n        \n        # Read object table entries\n        obj_table_start = le_offset + obj_table_off\n        print(f\"\\nObject Table at file offset 0x{obj_table_start:x}:\")\n        \n        for i in range(min(num_objects, 10)):\n            obj_entry = obj_table_start + i * 24  # Each entry is 24 bytes\n            if obj_entry + 24 &gt; len(data):\n                break\n            \n            virtual_size = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[obj_entry:obj_entry+4])[0]\n            reloc_base = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[obj_entry+4:obj_entry+8])[0]\n            obj_flags = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[obj_entry+8:obj_entry+12])[0]\n            page_map_index = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[obj_entry+12:obj_entry+16])[0]\n            page_map_entries = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[obj_entry+16:obj_entry+20])[0]\n            \n            print(f\"  Object {i+1}: size=0x{virtual_size:x}, base=0x{reloc_base:x}, \"\n                  f\"flags=0x{obj_flags:x}, page_idx={page_map_index}, pages={page_map_entries}\")\n    \n    # Based on typical DOS/4GW layout, try these offsets\n    print(\"\\n=== Trying various base calculations ===\")\n    \n    # Target virtual address\n    target_va = 0x47e58\n    \n    # Try different base assumptions\n    # For DOS/4GW, code typically starts at 0x10000\n    bases_to_try = [\n        (0x10000, \"Code object base 0x10000\"),\n        (0, \"Direct mapping\"),\n        (0x1000, \"Common base 0x1000\"),\n        (0x8000, \"Alternative base\"),\n    ]\n    \n    for base, desc in bases_to_try:\n        if target_va &gt;= base:\n            file_offset = target_va - base\n            if 0 &lt;= file_offset &lt; len(data):\n                sample = data[file_offset:file_offset+24]\n                print(f\"\\n{desc} -&gt; file offset 0x{file_offset:x}\")\n                print(f\"  Data: {sample.hex()}\")\n                \n                # Try parsing as dispatch table\n                entries = []\n                pos = file_offset\n                valid_looking = True\n                for j in range(10):\n                    if pos + 6 &gt; len(data):\n                        break\n                    action_id = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n                    handler = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n                    \n                    # Check if handler looks like a valid address\n                    if handler &gt; 0x50000 or (handler &lt; 0x10000 and handler != 0):\n                        valid_looking = False\n                        break\n                    \n                    if action_id == 0xFFFF:\n                        print(f\"  [Terminator at entry {j}]\")\n                        break\n                    entries.append((action_id, handler))\n                    pos += 6\n                    \n                if valid_looking and entries:\n                    print(f\"  Looks valid! First {min(5, len(entries))} entries:\")\n                    for k, (aid, h) in enumerate(entries[:5]):\n                        print(f\"    {k}: action={aid} (0x{aid:x}), handler=0x{h:x}\")\n                    \n                    # Search for action 273\n                    for aid, h in entries:\n                        if aid == 273:\n                            print(f\"\\n*** FOUND ACTION 273! Handler at 0x{h:x} ***\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    read_dispatch_table_from_exe()\n",

}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze F8 dispatch table with correct LE offset calculation.\nObject 2 (data) has base 0x40000 and starts at page 48.\nPage size is typically 4096 (0x1000).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\ndef analyze_le_exe():\n    exe_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/JUEGO.EXE\"\n    if not os.path.exists(exe_path):\n        print(f\"Cannot find {exe_path}\")\n        return\n    \n    with open(exe_path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"EXE size: {len(data)} bytes\")\n    \n    # Parse LE header\n    le_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[0x3C:0x3E])[0]\n    print(f\"LE header at 0x{le_offset:x}\")\n    \n    # Get data pages offset\n    data_pages_off = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[le_offset+0x80:le_offset+0x84])[0]\n    print(f\"Data pages start at file offset 0x{data_pages_off:x}\")\n    \n    # Object 2 starts at page 48, base address 0x40000\n    # Each page is 4096 bytes\n    # Page 48 -&gt; file offset = data_pages_off + (48-1) * 4096\n    \n    page_size = 4096\n    obj2_start_page = 48  # 1-indexed\n    obj2_file_offset = data_pages_off + (obj2_start_page - 1) * page_size\n    obj2_base_va = 0x40000\n    \n    print(f\"\\nObject 2 (data):\")\n    print(f\"  Base VA: 0x{obj2_base_va:x}\")\n    print(f\"  File offset: 0x{obj2_file_offset:x}\")\n    \n    # Target: 0x47e58 (in data object)\n    target_va = 0x47e58\n    offset_in_obj2 = target_va - obj2_base_va\n    file_offset = obj2_file_offset + offset_in_obj2\n    \n    print(f\"\\nTarget VA 0x{target_va:x}:\")\n    print(f\"  Offset in object 2: 0x{offset_in_obj2:x}\")\n    print(f\"  File offset: 0x{file_offset:x}\")\n    \n    if file_offset + 256 &gt; len(data):\n        print(\"ERROR: Calculated offset beyond file size\")\n        return\n    \n    # Read dispatch table\n    print(f\"\\n=== F8 Action Dispatch Table at 0x{target_va:x} ===\")\n    print(\"Format: [u16 action_id][u32 handler], 6 bytes each\")\n    \n    pos = file_offset\n    entries = []\n    for i in range(200):  # Max 200 entries\n        action_id = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n        handler = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n        \n        if action_id == 0xFFFF:\n            print(f\"\\n[Terminator at entry {i}]\")\n            break\n        \n        entries.append((action_id, handler))\n        \n        # Print first 20 entries and action 273\n        if i &lt; 20 or action_id == 273:\n            print(f\"Entry {i:3d}: action={action_id:4d} (0x{action_id:04x}), handler=0x{handler:08x}\")\n        \n        pos += 6\n    \n    print(f\"\\nTotal entries: {len(entries)}\")\n    \n    # Find action 273\n    print(\"\\n=== Searching for action 273 ===\")\n    for i, (aid, handler) in enumerate(entries):\n        if aid == 273:\n            print(f\"FOUND: Entry {i}, action 273 (0x111), handler at 0x{handler:08x}\")\n            # Read the handler code\n            handler_file_offset = handler - 0x10000 + data_pages_off  # Assuming handler is in code object\n            print(f\"Handler file offset: 0x{handler_file_offset:x}\")\n            if 0 &lt;= handler_file_offset &lt; len(data):\n                print(f\"Handler bytes: {data[handler_file_offset:handler_file_offset+32].hex()}\")\n            break\n    else:\n        print(\"Action 273 NOT FOUND in table\")\n        \n    # Print all actions in sorted order\n    print(\"\\n=== All actions sorted by ID ===\")\n    sorted_entries = sorted(entries, key=lambda x: x[0])\n    for aid, handler in sorted_entries:\n        if aid &gt;= 250 and aid &lt;= 300:  # Show range around 273\n            print(f\"  Action {aid:4d}: handler 0x{handler:08x}\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    analyze_le_exe()\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze SALVAJOC.006 save file and compare with ALFRED.1 to understand\nhow room state is persisted.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\ndef analyze_save_and_resource():\n    save_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/saves/SALVAJOC.006\"\n    alfred1_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/ALFRED.1\"\n    \n    if not os.path.exists(save_path):\n        print(f\"Cannot find {save_path}\")\n        return\n    \n    with open(save_path, 'rb') as f:\n        save_data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"=== Analyzing {save_path} ===\")\n    print(f\"File size: {len(save_data)} bytes\\n\")\n    \n    # Header\n    print(\"Header (first 64 bytes):\")\n    print(f\"  Magic: {save_data[0:16]}\")\n    print(f\"  Save name: {save_data[0x10:0x26]}\")\n    print(f\"  Room number: {save_data[0x26]}\")\n    print(f\"  Player X: {struct.unpack('&lt;H', save_data[0x28:0x2A])[0]}\")\n    print(f\"  Player Y: {struct.unpack('&lt;H', save_data[0x2A:0x2C])[0]}\")\n    \n    # Look for the walkbox data pattern mentioned: B4 01 64 01 04 00 0E 00 00\n    # Walkbox 1: x=436 (0x1B4), y=356 (0x164), w=4, h=14, flags=0\n    walkbox_pattern = bytes([0xB4, 0x01, 0x64, 0x01, 0x04, 0x00, 0x0E, 0x00, 0x00])\n    \n    print(f\"\\n=== Searching for walkbox pattern ===\")\n    print(f\"Pattern: {walkbox_pattern.hex()}\")\n    \n    pos = save_data.find(walkbox_pattern)\n    if pos != -1:\n        print(f\"Found at offset 0x{pos:x}\")\n        # Show surrounding context\n        print(f\"Context around pattern (20 bytes before, 30 after):\")\n        start = max(0, pos - 20)\n        end = min(len(save_data), pos + 30)\n        for i in range(start, end, 16):\n            line = save_data[i:i+16]\n            hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in line)\n            marker = \"  &lt;--\" if i &lt;= pos &lt; i + 16 else \"\"\n            print(f\"  0x{i:04x}: {hex_str}{marker}\")\n        \n        # Parse walkboxes at this location\n        print(f\"\\n=== Parsing walkboxes starting at 0x{pos:x} ===\")\n        wpos = pos\n        for i in range(5):  # Parse up to 5 walkboxes\n            if wpos + 9 &gt; len(save_data):\n                break\n            x = struct.unpack('&lt;H', save_data[wpos:wpos+2])[0]\n            y = struct.unpack('&lt;H', save_data[wpos+2:wpos+4])[0]\n            w = struct.unpack('&lt;H', save_data[wpos+4:wpos+6])[0]\n            h = struct.unpack('&lt;H', save_data[wpos+6:wpos+8])[0]\n            flags = save_data[wpos+8]\n            print(f\"  Walkbox {i}: x={x}, y={y}, w={w}, h={h}, flags={flags}\")\n            wpos += 9\n    else:\n        print(\"Pattern not found!\")\n        \n    # Also check if the save file contains ALFRED.1 room data directly\n    # Look for room 14 marker\n    print(f\"\\n=== Save file structure analysis ===\")\n    \n    # The save file seems to store state for all rooms\n    # Let's look for patterns that indicate room data boundaries\n    \n    # Look for the second walkbox pattern: B8 01 70 01 94 00 02 00 00\n    # Walkbox 2: x=440 (0x1B8), y=368 (0x170), w=148 (0x94), h=2\n    walkbox2_pattern = bytes([0xB8, 0x01, 0x70, 0x01, 0x94, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0x00])\n    pos2 = save_data.find(walkbox2_pattern)\n    if pos2 != -1:\n        print(f\"Second walkbox pattern found at 0x{pos2:x}\")\n        # This should be 9 bytes after the first\n        if pos != -1:\n            print(f\"  Distance from first: {pos2 - pos} bytes (expected 9)\")\n    \n    # Now check ALFRED.1 for comparison\n    if os.path.exists(alfred1_path):\n        with open(alfred1_path, 'rb') as f:\n            alfred1_data = f.read()\n        \n        print(f\"\\n=== Checking ALFRED.1 ===\")\n        print(f\"File size: {len(alfred1_data)} bytes\")\n        \n        # Search for the same walkbox patterns\n        pos_a1 = alfred1_data.find(walkbox_pattern)\n        if pos_a1 != -1:\n            print(f\"Walkbox pattern found in ALFRED.1 at 0x{pos_a1:x}\")\n        else:\n            print(\"Walkbox pattern NOT found in ALFRED.1 (expected - these are added by action)\")\n    \n    # Check save file for room count / room index data\n    print(f\"\\n=== Examining potential room state offsets ===\")\n    \n    # Check bytes at known offsets from your analysis\n    # 0x25F1 mentioned as walkbox data offset\n    if 0x25F1 &lt; len(save_data):\n        print(f\"Data at offset 0x25F1: {save_data[0x25F1:0x25F1+20].hex()}\")\n    \n    # Check if save stores room 14 state specifically\n    # Room 14 = 0x0E\n    print(f\"\\n=== Looking for room 14 (0x0E) references ===\")\n    for i in range(0x100, min(0x400, len(save_data))):\n        if save_data[i] == 14:\n            context = save_data[max(0,i-2):i+10]\n            print(f\"  0x{i:04x}: {context.hex()}\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    analyze_save_and_resource()\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nDeep analysis of save game structure to understand how room state is saved.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\ndef analyze_save_deep():\n    save_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/saves/SALVAJOC.006\"\n    \n    with open(save_path, 'rb') as f:\n        save_data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"=== Deep analysis of {save_path} ===\")\n    print(f\"File size: {len(save_data)} bytes (0x{len(save_data):x})\\n\")\n    \n    # The walkbox data starts at 0x25F1\n    # But what's the structure before it?\n    \n    # Look at data leading up to walkboxes\n    print(\"=== Data before walkbox region (0x25D0 - 0x25F1) ===\")\n    for i in range(0x25D0, 0x25F1, 8):\n        chunk = save_data[i:i+8]\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in chunk)\n        print(f\"  0x{i:04x}: {hex_str}\")\n    \n    # Look at what appears to be a pattern: XX 01 FA 0E 00 YY ZZ 01\n    # This looks like it could be room state entries\n    print(\"\\n=== Analyzing potential room state entries ===\")\n    print(\"Pattern appears to be: [?] [01] [FA] [room?] [00] [??] [??] [01]\")\n    \n    # Let's look for all occurrences of \"FA 0E\" (0xFA = disabled marker?, 0x0E = room 14?)\n    pos = 0\n    occurrences = []\n    while True:\n        pos = save_data.find(b'\\xfa\\x0e', pos)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        occurrences.append(pos)\n        pos += 1\n    \n    print(f\"\\nFound {len(occurrences)} occurrences of FA 0E:\")\n    for occ in occurrences[:20]:\n        context = save_data[max(0, occ-4):occ+8]\n        print(f\"  0x{occ:04x}: {context.hex()}\")\n    \n    # The structure seems to be per-room state records\n    # Let's look for room 14 specifically (0x0E)\n    print(\"\\n=== Looking for per-room state data ===\")\n    \n    # Search for patterns that look like [room_id] [data...]\n    # Typical room numbers are 0-55 (0x37)\n    \n    # Look at 0x25E0 region more carefully\n    print(\"\\nExamining region 0x25E0-0x2650:\")\n    for i in range(0x25E0, min(0x2650, len(save_data)), 16):\n        chunk = save_data[i:i+16]\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in chunk)\n        # Try to interpret as walkbox if it looks like one\n        if i &gt;= 0x25F1:\n            # Parse as walkbox\n            x = struct.unpack('&lt;H', save_data[i:i+2])[0]\n            y = struct.unpack('&lt;H', save_data[i+2:i+4])[0]\n            if x &lt; 640 and y &lt; 480:  # Screen bounds check\n                interpretation = f\" (Walkbox? x={x}, y={y})\"\n            else:\n                interpretation = \"\"\n        else:\n            interpretation = \"\"\n        print(f\"  0x{i:04x}: {hex_str}{interpretation}\")\n    \n    # Now let's look at the overall save structure\n    print(\"\\n=== Save file section analysis ===\")\n    \n    # Header section: 0x00-0x27\n    print(\"Header (0x00-0x27):\")\n    print(f\"  Magic: {save_data[0:16]}\")\n    print(f\"  Save name: {save_data[0x10:0x26]}\")\n    print(f\"  Room: {save_data[0x26]}\")\n    \n    # What comes after header?\n    print(\"\\nPost-header (0x28-0x100):\")\n    for i in range(0x28, 0x100, 16):\n        chunk = save_data[i:i+16]\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in chunk)\n        print(f\"  0x{i:04x}: {hex_str}\")\n    \n    # Look for inventory data\n    print(\"\\n=== Looking for inventory section ===\")\n    # Inventory typically has item IDs (small numbers)\n    # Let's search for known item ID patterns\n    \n    # Look at the region around 0x100-0x200\n    print(\"Region 0x100-0x200:\")\n    for i in range(0x100, 0x200, 16):\n        chunk = save_data[i:i+16]\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in chunk)\n        print(f\"  0x{i:04x}: {hex_str}\")\n    \n    #   "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze ALFRED.8 - appears to be small (649 bytes)\nWhat is it storing?\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\ndef analyze_alfred8():\n    alfred8_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/ALFRED.8\"\n    \n    with open(alfred8_path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"=== ALFRED.8 Analysis ===\")\n    print(f\"File size: {len(data)} bytes\\n\")\n    \n    # Dump entire file\n    print(\"Complete hex dump of ALFRED.8:\")\n    for i in range(0, len(data), 16):\n        chunk = data[i:i+16]\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in chunk)\n        ascii_str = ''.join(chr(b) if 32 &lt;= b &lt; 127 else '.' for b in chunk)\n        print(f\"  0x{i:04x}: {hex_str:48s}  {ascii_str}\")\n    \n    # Try to interpret structure\n    print(\"\\n=== Structure interpretation ===\")\n    \n    # First try as list of offsets/values\n    print(\"As 16-bit values:\")\n    for i in range(0, min(64, len(data)), 2):\n        val = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[i:i+2])[0]\n        print(f\"  0x{i:03x}: {val} (0x{val:04x})\")\n    \n    print(\"\\nAs 32-bit values:\")\n    for i in range(0, min(64, len(data)), 4):\n        val = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[i:i+4])[0]\n        print(f\"  0x{i:03x}: {val} (0x{val:08x})\")\n    \n    # Check if it could be sound/music configuration  \n    # Or perhaps room initialization data\n    \n    # Look for patterns\n    print(\"\\n=== Pattern analysis ===\")\n    \n    # Count byte frequencies\n    freq = {}\n    for b in data:\n        freq[b] = freq.get(b, 0) + 1\n    \n    common = sorted(freq.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:10]\n    print(\"Most common bytes:\")\n    for b, count in common:\n        print(f\"  0x{b:02x}: {count} times\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    analyze_alfred8()\n",
